Class PropertyDefinition<T>

java.lang.Object
dev.tamboui.style.PropertyDefinition<T>
Type Parameters:
T - the type of value this property definition represents
public final class PropertyDefinition<T> extends Object
A typed definition for a style property, bundling the property name with its converter, inheritance behavior, and optional default value.

PropertyDefinitions are typically defined as constants in property registry classes: 

public static final PropertyDefinition<Color> COLOR =
    PropertyDefinition.builder("color", ColorConverter.INSTANCE)
        .inheritable()
        .build();

public static final PropertyDefinition<Color> BACKGROUND =
    PropertyDefinition.of("background", ColorConverter.INSTANCE); // Non-inheritable

They can then be used with StylePropertyResolver to retrieve typed values: 

Color color = resolver.get(BORDER_COLOR).orElse(Color.WHITE);

    • isInheritable

      public boolean isInheritable()
      Returns whether this property is inherited from parent elements.

      Per CSS semantics, inheritable properties (like color, text-style) are passed from parent to child elements if not explicitly set.

      Returns:
      true if this property inherits from parent
